<meta>continues from previous page</meta>he returns within those seven days. For that monk, bhikkhus, the earlier <term>vassa</term> <gloss>rainy season retreat</gloss> is recognized and there is no offense regarding the undertaking. 6

In another case, monks, he departs on account of some business seven days before the <term>Pavāranā</term> <gloss>the ceremony marking the end of the retreat</gloss>. Whether that monk returns to that residence or does not return, bhikkhus, for that monk the earlier retreat is recognized and there is no offense regarding the undertaking. 7

In another case, monks, a monk has promised to observe the rainy season retreat during the earlier period. Having gone to that residence, he performs the <term>Uposatha</term> <gloss>observance day rites</gloss>, enters the monastery on the day after the full moon, prepares his lodging, sets out water for drinking and washing, and sweeps the courtyard. He then departs on that very day for no particular business. For that monk, bhikkhus, the earlier retreat is not recognized and there is an offense of <term>dukkata</term> <gloss>wrongdoing</gloss> regarding the undertaking. 8

In another case <note>repeat of section 8</note> he departs on that very day for some business <note>the text indicates an omission here</note> he departs after staying two or three days for no particular business <note>the text indicates an omission here</note> he departs after staying two or three days for some business <note>the text indicates an omission here</note> he departs after staying two or three days on some business to be completed within seven days. He spends those seven days outside. For that monk, bhikkhus, the earlier retreat is not recognized and there is an offense of wrongdoing regarding the undertaking. 9

He departs after staying two or three days on some business to be completed within seven days. He returns within those seven days. For that monk, bhikkhus, the earlier retreat is recognized and there is no offense regarding the undertaking. He departs seven days <note>repeat of section 7</note> there is no offense. 10

In another case, monks, a monk has promised to observe the rainy season retreat during the later period. While going to that residence, he performs the observance day rites outside, enters the monastery on the day after the full moon, prepares his lodging, sets out water for drinking and washing, and sweeps the courtyard. He then departs on that very day for no particular business. For that monk, bhikkhus, the later retreat is not recognized and there is an offense of wrongdoing regarding the undertaking. In another case <note>the whole passage is identical with sections 5 to 10; read instead of "earlier" and "the earlier": "later" and "the later"; and instead of "before the Pavāranā": "before the Komudi full moon of the fourth month"</note> there is no offense regarding the undertaking. 11 14

The Third Chapter, the <term>Vassūpanāyikakkhandhaka</term> <gloss>Chapter on Entering the Rainy Season Retreat</gloss>, is concluded.

Its summary:
Entering, and when, how many, during the rains,
and if they do not wish, intentionally, to postpone, a lay follower.

<summary>This page concludes the regulations regarding the two periods for the rainy season retreat, detailing the conditions under which a monk's undertaking of the retreat is considered valid or invalid when he departs for business. It also provides a mnemonic summary for the entire chapter.</summary>
